name: Kerala Piravi lunch at home
description: On 1 November, Kerala homes post the Piravi lunch at their own table rather than out. Couples dress in kasavu and mundu and are photographed together just before eating, late morning to early afternoon. Weekday posts show red rice, thoran and sambar on steel plates with the nilavilakku lit; weekend posts move to a banana-leaf spread. Coconut trees through the window and red oxide floors recur.

name: Golu mornings in Chennai
description: During Navratri, Chennai posts open on the Golu steps in early morning light, then cut to the kitchen as breakfast is made: dosa on an iron tawa, sambar simmering. Guests arrive from late afternoon, so the morning is the quiet family moment. Sundal is the Golu offering; silk sarees appear in the evening posts, cotton in the morning ones.

name: Diwali-week lunch prep in Delhi
description: In the week before Diwali, Delhi kitchens post late-morning lunch prep with a parent visiting: phulkas puffing on the flame, dal on the stove, diyas being set out in the background. Festival sweets sit in boxes on the counter, apart from the everyday meal. Posts cluster between 11 am and 1 pm, with marble floors and a mandir niche in frame.

name: Winter Sunday lunch in Punjab
description: From December to January, Ludhiana and Amritsar families post long Sunday lunches at the dining table: rotis from a steel dabba, dal, sabzi and raita, lassi and chai in steel glasses, shawls on the shoulders. Three generations at one table is the common frame; children stay in the background. Around Lohri, the bonfire posts are evening, the food posts are lunch.

name: Weekday dabba in Mumbai
description: Mumbai weekday posts show the lunch dabba packed between 7 and 8 am in a compact flat kitchen: poli, bhaji and varan-bhaat in steel tiffin tiers, office ID already round the neck. The same people post the opened dabba at a desk around 1 pm. Grill windows and a mandir shelf recur in the morning frames.

name: Reading labels in November
description: Across North and West India in November, people post themselves reading food labels at home in the evening, usually at the dining table after work, with a spouse looking on. Pune and Ahmedabad posts are the most common. The frame is close on hands and the back of the pack under warm indoor light, followed by dinner being served.
